modes.label: Idea Mode
modes.hint: Explore possibilities before choosing a path.

modes.label: Tool Mode
modes.hint: Turn information into a useful output.

modes.label: Practice Mode
modes.hint: Rehearse a situation before real life.

safetyLenses.label: Tune the Prompt
safetyLenses.hint: Add task, context, format, limits, or audience.

safetyLenses.label: Keep It Private
safetyLenses.hint: Remove names, passwords, records, and personal details.

safetyLenses.label: Check the Claim
safetyLenses.hint: Verify facts, quotes, sources, dates, and current information.

safetyLenses.label: Make It Fair
safetyLenses.hint: Watch for bias, overreliance, disclosure, and honest use.

boardSpaces.label: Construction Detour
boardSpaces.complication: The first answer sounds useful, but it skips an important limit.

boardSpaces.label: Shortcut Bridge
boardSpaces.complication: Before the reveal, the crew may wager one Mile Token on the explanation.

boardSpaces.label: Merge Lane
boardSpaces.complication: Another player may ride shotgun by adding one improvement before the vote.

scenarioCards.title: Science Fair Start
scenarioCards.scenario: Your group needs a science fair project that fits your time, materials, and interests.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Idea Mode helps the crew generate several possible project directions before choosing one.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Learning Mode works if the first need is understanding the science topics before brainstorming.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: Do not let AI pick the whole project without checking what the group can actually build.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: What kind of AI help would you choose first?

scenarioCards.title: History Poster
scenarioCards.scenario: A student has a history poster topic but the first AI answer is too vague to use.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Feedback Mode helps improve the draft direction without taking over the poster.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Tune the Prompt matters if the crew names audience, format, limits, and facts to check.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: A confident answer can still include facts that need verification.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: How should the crew ask for help without asking AI to finish the work?

scenarioCards.title: Club Announcement
scenarioCards.scenario: The robotics club needs a short announcement for the morning bulletin.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Tool Mode fits because the crew is turning known details into a useful format.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Feedback Mode works if there is already a rough announcement to improve.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: Make sure names, meeting details, and permission-sensitive information are safe to share.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: What information should be included, and what should stay private?

scenarioCards.title: Difficult Conversation
scenarioCards.scenario: A student wants to practice asking a teacher for help after missing several assignments.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Practice Mode fits because the student can rehearse respectful words before real life.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Feedback Mode works if the student already wrote a message and wants it improved.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: The message should sound like the student, not like a fake adult script.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: What would be useful to practice before the real conversation?

scenarioCards.title: Current Event Claim
scenarioCards.scenario: AI gives a strong-sounding explanation of a current event for class discussion.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Learning Mode can help explain the topic, but Check the Claim should guide the turn.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Tool Mode works if the crew makes a source-checking list before using the explanation.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: Current events change quickly, so date, source, and evidence matter.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: What should the crew verify before trusting the answer?

scenarioCards.title: Study Plan
scenarioCards.scenario: A student has a quiz in three days and wants a simple plan for studying.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Tool Mode fits because AI can organize the available time into a practical plan.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Learning Mode works if the student needs concepts explained before planning.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: The plan should match the actual class notes, not replace studying.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: What details would make the plan realistic?

scenarioCards.title: Group Slide Deck
scenarioCards.scenario: A team has notes for a presentation but needs help turning them into clear slides.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Tool Mode helps organize the notes into headings, order, and speaker cues.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Feedback Mode works if a draft deck already exists.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: AI should not invent evidence or make one group member's work disappear.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: What should the crew provide so the slides stay accurate?

scenarioCards.title: Book Reflection
scenarioCards.scenario: A student needs to write a reflection on a book chapter they actually read.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Idea Mode can help brainstorm angles while the student keeps the real reflection.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Feedback Mode works if the student brings their own rough paragraph first.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: The reflection should not pretend AI read or felt the chapter for the student.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: How can AI support the student's thinking without replacing it?

scenarioCards.title: Community Survey
scenarioCards.scenario: A class wants to summarize survey responses about improving the school courtyard.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Tool Mode fits because AI can help group and summarize responses.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Make It Fair matters if the crew checks whose voices might be missing.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: Names and private details should be removed before using AI.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: What should be removed or checked before summarizing?

scenarioCards.title: Interview Practice
scenarioCards.scenario: A student wants to prepare for a short interview about joining a youth program.
scenarioCards.likelyStrong: Practice Mode fits because AI can simulate questions and help the student rehearse.
scenarioCards.alsoWorksIf: Feedback Mode works if the student already has draft answers.
scenarioCards.watchOutFor: Practice should build confidence, not create answers the student cannot explain.
scenarioCards.discussionPrompt: What kind of rehearsal would make the student more ready?

roadMoveCards.title: Add the Missing Details
roadMoveCards.prompt: Name the task, audience, format, and limits before asking for AI help.
roadMoveCards.likelyStrong: A tuned prompt gives AI enough direction while keeping the human goal clear.
roadMoveCards.alsoWorksIf: The crew can also ask AI what details are missing before sending a full prompt.
roadMoveCards.watchOutFor: A vague prompt can produce a vague answer that looks more useful than it is.
roadMoveCards.discussionPrompt: What one detail would improve the prompt most?

roadMoveCards.title: Use an Example
roadMoveCards.prompt: Add one example of the style, level, or format you want.
roadMoveCards.likelyStrong: An example helps the AI match the desired output without guessing.
roadMoveCards.alsoWorksIf: A checklist of must-have parts can work when there is no example.
roadMoveCards.watchOutFor: The example should guide the answer, not become copied work.
roadMoveCards.discussionPrompt: What example would make this request clearer?

roadMoveCards.title: Remove Private Details
roadMoveCards.prompt: Strip names, accounts, records, addresses, and unnecessary personal details.
roadMoveCards.likelyStrong: Private information should be removed before using an AI tool.
roadMoveCards.alsoWorksIf: The crew can replace sensitive details with placeholders like Student A or School Event.
roadMoveCards.watchOutFor: If the detail is not needed for the task, do not share it.
roadMoveCards.discussionPrompt: What detail should be removed first?

roadMoveCards.title: Share Only What Is Needed
roadMoveCards.prompt: Use the smallest amount of information needed to get useful help.
roadMoveCards.likelyStrong: Limiting context reduces privacy risk while still supporting the task.
roadMoveCards.alsoWorksIf: A teacher-approved tool or offline discussion may be better for sensitive cases.
roadMoveCards.watchOutFor: Convenience is not a reason to paste private records into a tool.
roadMoveCards.discussionPrompt: What does AI actually need to know here?

roadMoveCards.title: Verify the Source
roadMoveCards.prompt: Name what fact, quote, date, or source should be checked before trusting the answer.
roadMoveCards.likelyStrong: Important claims should be verified against reliable sources.
roadMoveCards.alsoWorksIf: The crew can ask AI to list claims that need checking, then verify outside the tool.
roadMoveCards.watchOutFor: AI can sound confident while being wrong or outdated.
roadMoveCards.discussionPrompt: Which claim matters enough to check?

roadMoveCards.title: Find the Evidence
roadMoveCards.prompt: Ask what evidence would prove or weaken the answer.
roadMoveCards.likelyStrong: Evidence keeps the crew from accepting a claim just because it sounds polished.
roadMoveCards.alsoWorksIf: A source date or author check can be enough for a quick classroom turn.
roadMoveCards.watchOutFor: A list of sources from AI still needs real checking.
roadMoveCards.discussionPrompt: What evidence would make this answer more trustworthy?

roadMoveCards.title: Keep the Human Voice
roadMoveCards.prompt: Explain how the final work will stay honest and human-owned.
roadMoveCards.likelyStrong: The player should keep responsibility for the decision, voice, and final work.
roadMoveCards.alsoWorksIf: Disclosure or teacher rules can guide how AI support is used.
roadMoveCards.watchOutFor: AI support becomes unfair when it hides authorship or replaces learning.
roadMoveCards.discussionPrompt: What part must stay the student's own work?

roadMoveCards.title: Check Who Is Missing
roadMoveCards.prompt: Look for missing perspectives, bias, or people affected by the answer.
roadMoveCards.likelyStrong: Fair use means noticing who benefits, who is left out, and what impact the answer has.
roadMoveCards.alsoWorksIf: The crew can ask for counterexamples or perspectives to review critically.
roadMoveCards.watchOutFor: More polished wording can hide an unfair or incomplete idea.
roadMoveCards.discussionPrompt: Whose perspective should the crew consider?

hazardCards.title: Construction Zone Prompt
hazardCards.scenario: The crew asked AI for help, but the request only said, "help with my project."
hazardCards.complication: The answer is messy because the request is missing topic, audience, format, and limits.
hazardCards.likelyStrong: Tune the Prompt is the strongest safety move because the request needs direction first.
hazardCards.alsoWorksIf: Learning Mode can work if the crew uses the moment to learn what a better prompt needs.
hazardCards.watchOutFor: Do not blame the tool before checking whether the request was clear.
hazardCards.discussionPrompt: What detail would clear the construction zone?

hazardCards.title: Privacy Pothole
hazardCards.scenario: The useful example includes a student's name, schedule, and family detail.
hazardCards.complication: The crew must remove personal details before asking for help.
hazardCards.likelyStrong: Keep It Private is the strongest safety move because the risk is unnecessary personal information.
hazardCards.alsoWorksIf: Tool Mode can work after the private details are replaced with placeholders.
hazardCards.watchOutFor: A good answer is not worth sharing sensitive information.
hazardCards.discussionPrompt: What should be changed before the crew continues?

hazardCards.title: Foggy Fact
hazardCards.scenario: AI gives a neat statistic, but nobody knows where it came from.
hazardCards.complication: The crew must decide what evidence would make the statistic usable.
hazardCards.likelyStrong: Check the Claim is strongest because the answer needs source, date, and evidence.
hazardCards.alsoWorksIf: Learning Mode can work if the crew treats the statistic as a question to investigate.
hazardCards.watchOutFor: A statistic without a source can steer the whole answer wrong.
hazardCards.discussionPrompt: What proof would clear the fog?

hazardCards.title: Unfair Shortcut
hazardCards.scenario: AI offers to write the final answer in a way that hides the student's role.
hazardCards.complication: The crew needs a fair support move, not a replacement for the student's work.
hazardCards.likelyStrong: Make It Fair is strongest because the issue is honesty, authorship, and learning.
hazardCards.alsoWorksIf: Feedback Mode can work if the student brings their own draft first.
hazardCards.watchOutFor: A polished answer can still be unfair if it hides who did the thinking.
hazardCards.discussionPrompt: What support would be fair instead?

finalChallenge.title: Green Light Gate
finalChallenge.scenario: The crew reaches the city gate. Choose one real AI help move for a school, home, or community task and explain how to use it responsibly.
finalChallenge.likelyStrong: A gate answer names the help type, gives a reason, chooses a Road Move, and names one risk.
finalChallenge.alsoWorksIf: Different modes can work if the crew explains the need and handles the risk.
finalChallenge.watchOutFor: Do not treat the permit as proof of mastery. It is a playful completion marker.
finalChallenge.discussionPrompt: What AI help fits, and what keeps it responsible?
